target.statement: Consensus anomaly detection yields 6 consensus anomalies (7.7% of 78 samples), all at Site S3, with Isolation Forest and PCA reconstruction error each flagging 12 samples (15.4%) and DBSCAN flagging none
target.table_ref: Fig. IV.4 anomaly count matrix / Section IV-B text
target.dataset: Soil heavy metal concentrations (As, Cd, Cr, Cu, Hg, Ni, Pb, Zn) for 78 samples from 12 waste sites + residential controls, Central Region, Ghana

compute.basis: The pipeline is scikit-learn IsolationForest/DBSCAN/PCA on a 78x8 table; the only real cost is re-entering the raw data, which is not published.

blockers: Raw per-sample heavy metal concentrations (78 samples x 8 metals) are not provided in the paper or any linked repository; only summary statistics (Table I) and figures are given
No code or data links in the PDF
HI/ILCR validation requires per-sample exposure parameters not tabulated
title: Anomaly Detection in Soil Heavy Metal Contamination Using Unsupervised Learning for Environmental Risk Assessment
